description.narrative: In August 2021, the Government of Sierra Leone submitted its outstanding reports on the application of International Labour Standards according to Article 22. The reports on Conventions C29, C105, 138, 182, C100, C111, 81, 26, 95, 99, 101, 45, 119, 17, 19, 94, 22, 125, 126 and 32. The Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MLSS) in collaboration with the social partners organised a capacity-building workshop in August 2021 for the tripartite plus partners and the information gathered at the workshop was used to finalise the reports. The ILO reinforced the capacity of the tripartite partners on drafting the reports. The tripartite partners attended different online training sessions organised by ITC/ILO on International Labour Standards in October/November 2020 and in February 2021.

description.narrative: In August 2021, the Government of Sierra Leone through the Permanent Mission in Geneva deposited the ratification instrument for the ratification of Protocol of 2014 to the Forced Labour Convention 1930 (P.029). The ratification is the first in the ratification of ILO Conventions since 2011 and the Government has shown a commitment to protect workers from all forms of forced labour and trafficking in persons. The ILO provided technical comments to the assessment for the ratification of P.029. In addition, the ILO held a series of meetings from January to July 2021 with the different Ministers and with relevant stakeholders so as to provide guidance on the deposition of the ratification instruments.

description.narrative: The Government of Sierra Leone has ratified and deposited the ratification instruments for seven technical conventions of the ILO. This was registered with the ILO on 25 August 2021 and the 8 conventions are: the Migration for Employment Convention (Revised), 1949 (No. 97); the Migrant Workers (Supplementary Provisions) Convention, 1975 (No. 143); the Labour Administration Convention, 1978 (No. 150); the Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 1981 (No. 155); the Private Employment Agencies Convention, 1997 (No. 181); the Promotional Framework for Occupational Safety and Health Convention, 2006 (No. 187); the Domestic Workers Convention, 2011 (No. 189). No technical conventions has been ratified by Sierra Leone since 1967, more than 50 years ago. These ratifications will provide a favourable environment for the adoption of a modern legislative framework conducive to decent work for all. The ILO provided technical comments on the draft Labour Act consolidating different pieces of legislation that had been discussed by the Joint Consultative Committee that led to the ratifications. In addition, the ILO held a series of meetings from January to July 2021 with the different Ministers and with relevant stakeholders so as to provide guidance on the deposition of the ratification instruments.
